name: Very Plain Mince-Meat
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: lean beef and one pound fat beef
ingredients.originalText: two pounds lean beef and one pound fat beef

ingredients.name: one quart bottled or sweet cider
ingredients.originalText: one quart bottled or sweet cider
ingredients.quantityText: one quart bottled or sweet cider

instructions.text: Take a piece of fresh beef, consisting of about two pounds of lean, and one pound of fat.
Boil it, and when it is quite cold, chop it fine.
Or you may substitute cold roast beef.
Pare and core some fine juicy apples, cut them in pieces, weigh three pounds, and chop them.
Stone four pounds of raisins, and chop them also.
Add a large table-spoonful of powdered cloves, and the same quantity of powdered cinnamon.
Also a pound of brown sugar.
Mix all thoroughly, moistening it with a quart of bottled or sweet cider.
You may add the grated peel and the juice of an orange.
Bake it in good common paste.

source.originalInstructions:
1. Take a piece of fresh beef, consisting of about two pounds of lean, and one pound of fat.
2. Boil it, and when it is quite cold, chop it fine.
3. Or you may substitute cold roast beef.
4. Pare and core some fine juicy apples, cut them in pieces, weigh three pounds, and chop them.
5. Stone four pounds of raisins, and chop them also.
6. Add a large table-spoonful of powdered cloves, and the same quantity of powdered cinnamon.
7. Also a pound of brown sugar.
8. Mix all thoroughly, moistening it with a quart of bottled or sweet cider.
9. You may add the grated peel and the juice of an orange.
10. Bake it in good common paste.
